guide.title: Ledyard, Connecticut: Farm Town Turned Resort Destination
guide.intro: Ledyard incorporated as a town in 1836, taking its name from Colonel William Ledyard, the Revolutionary War officer killed defending Fort Griswold on Groton Heights in 1781. Settlement in the area reaches back to the mid-seventeenth century, chronicled in John Avery's 1901 history of the town's first 250 years. A farming community through the nineteenth century, Ledyard later became a bedroom community for workers commuting to Groton and New London along the Thames. Its modern era turned on a single 1992 decision: the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation opened Foxwoods Resort Casino in the town's northeastern section, and it grew into one of Connecticut's biggest tourist draws. The tribally owned Mashantucket Pequot Museum and Research Center followed in 1998, billed as the world's largest Native American museum. Older industry survives too, at the town-owned Ledyard Up-Down Sawmill, a rare water-powered sash mill restored to working order in the 1970s.

sections.heading: Farm town turned resort destination
sections.body: Ledyard incorporated as a town in 1836, taking its name from Colonel William Ledyard, the Revolutionary War officer killed defending Fort Griswold on Groton Heights in 1781. Settlement in the area reaches back to the mid-seventeenth century, chronicled in John Avery's 1901 history of the town's first 250 years. A farming community through the nineteenth century, Ledyard later became a bedroom community for workers commuting to Groton and New London along the Thames. Its modern era turned on a single 1992 decision: the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation opened Foxwoods Resort Casino in the town's northeastern section, and it grew into one of Connecticut's biggest tourist draws. The tribally owned Mashantucket Pequot Museum and Research Center followed in 1998, billed as the world's largest Native American museum.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Ledyard is a driving destination: travelers exit I-95 on the Groton/North Stonington side (Exit 88) and follow local roads such as Colonel Ledyard Highway and CT Route 214 into town. There is no rail station in Ledyard itself — the nearest trains are at New London Union Station, served by Amtrak Northeast Regional and Acela and the eastern terminus of CTrail's Shore Line East commuter line.

sections.heading: Foxwoods, a sawmill, and a family winery
sections.body: Foxwoods Resort Casino, opened by the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation in 1992, anchors the town's northeastern section with gaming, dining, and hotel towers including the Grand Pequot Tower. The town-owned Ledyard Up-Down Sawmill, at Sawmill Park on Route 214, is a rare surviving water-powered up-and-down sash sawmill, demonstrated by volunteers on spring and fall Saturdays. Maugle Sierra Vineyards and Holmberg Orchards & Winery Farm Market round out a more rural side of town, both reached from I-95 Exit 88.

faq.question: How do I get to Ledyard?
faq.answer: Ledyard is a driving destination reached from I-95 Exit 88 via Colonel Ledyard Highway and CT Route 214. There is no rail station in Ledyard; the nearest is New London Union Station, served by Amtrak Northeast Regional, Acela, and Shore Line East's eastern terminus.

faq.question: When did Foxwoods Resort Casino open?
faq.answer: The Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation opened Foxwoods in 1992 in the northeastern section of Ledyard; it has since grown into one of Connecticut's biggest tourist destinations, with hotel towers including the Grand Pequot Tower and Fox Tower.

faq.question: What is the Mashantucket Pequot Museum and Research Center?
faq.answer: A tribally owned museum that opened August 11, 1998, described as the world's largest Native American museum. Open Wednesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m.

faq.question: What is the Ledyard Up-Down Sawmill?
faq.answer: A rare surviving water-powered up-and-down (sash) sawmill at Sawmill Park on Route 214, restored to operating condition in the 1970s and still run by volunteers, with free demonstrations on Saturdays 1-4 p.m. in spring (April-May) and fall (October-November).

faq.question: Is there lodging in Ledyard outside of Foxwoods?
faq.answer: The only lodging verified inside Ledyard's boundaries is the Foxwoods resort hotel complex on the Mashantucket Pequot reservation; no independent inn or B&B in town could be verified as currently operating.

places.name: Mashantucket Pequot Museum and Research Center
places.summary: Tribally owned and operated since opening August 11, 1998; described as the world's largest Native American museum. Open Wednesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m.

places.name: Ledyard Up-Down Sawmill (Sawmill Park)
places.address: Sawmill Park, 172 Iron St. (Route 214), Ledyard, CT
places.summary: A rare surviving water-powered up-and-down (sash) sawmill, restored in the 1970s and owned by the town; the park also holds a blacksmith shop, circular sawmill, shingle machine, gristmill, and ice-harvesting exhibits. Free admission; volunteer-run demonstrations Saturdays 1-4 p.m. in spring (April-May) and fall (October-November).

places.name: Foxwoods Resort Casino
places.summary: Opened by the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation in 1992 in the northeastern section of Ledyard; a resort complex of gaming, entertainment, and dining with three main hotel towers — Grand Pequot Tower, Fox Tower, and Great Cedar Hotel.

places.name: Maugle Sierra Vineyards
places.summary: A working winery and event venue offering tastings, live music, and weddings; reached from I-95 Exit 88. Tasting room hours Friday 2-6 p.m., Saturday-Sunday 12-6 p.m.

places.name: Nathan Lester House and Farm Tool Museum
places.address: 153 Vinegar Hill Road, Gales Ferry, CT 06335
places.summary: A historic house and farm-tool museum maintained by the Ledyard Historical Society; specific 2026 open hours were not posted, so call (860) 464-2040 ahead — it traditionally opens seasonally.

places.name: Holmberg Orchards & Winery Farm Market
places.summary: A local-institution farm market with an in-house bakery, prepared foods, and its own winery and cidery, plus seasonal pick-your-own fruit and lavender products. Farm market open year-round daily 9 a.m.-6 p.m.

places.name: Cedars Steaks & Oysters
places.summary: Foxwoods' signature tribally owned steak-and-seafood house, one of the resort's longest-running fine-dining rooms.

places.name: Grand Pequot Tower at Foxwoods Resort Casino
places.summary: The flagship AAA Four Diamond-class tower of the Foxwoods resort complex, opened by the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation whose casino sits in the northeastern section of Ledyard.
